note: D5. Q asks for the caller procedure that makes Cobra deal with a single-dash long option token `-delete` the way git does. At the pin, Cobra performs no flag-token parsing of its own: command.go:30 aliases the dependency `github.com/spf13/pflag` as `flag`, and ParseFlags (command.go:1818-1840) hands the raw argument slice straight to `c.Flags().Parse(args)` at command.go:1833; README.md:77-79 says "Flag functionality is provided by the [pflag library] ... which maintains the same interface while adding POSIX compliance." pflag v1.0.5 (go.mod:8) is not tracked in the pinned tree: `git ls-files` at the pin lists 66 files and none of them is pflag or vendored source. The Cobra-side code that does look at single-dash tokens does not bind them to long flag names: stripFlags (command.go:642-679) treats a single-dash token as a flag only when `len(s) == 2` (command.go:664), i.e. `-d`, and it only removes args for subcommand lookup rather than defining flag syntax; argsMinusFirstX (command.go:684 onward) repeats the same test. The other Cobra knobs I checked are related but do not contain the requested mechanism: SetGlobalNormalizationFunc (command.go:362-372) normalizes flag names inside pflag's flag sets and does not change dash syntax; FParseErrWhitelist (command.go:199-200, applied at command.go:1831) only suppresses unknown-flag errors; DisableFlagParsing (command.go:236-238, honoured at command.go:1820-1822 and command.go:932-934) merely forwards every token to the command as arguments and names neither `-delete` nor any git-like handling, so citing it as the answer would be a generic escape hatch plus the unstated premise - supplied by pflag, not by the cited bytes - that `-delete` is otherwise rejected. I therefore find related code but no contiguous span in a tracked, regular .go file at the pin that contains the mechanism or ordered steps Q expressly asks for; writing one would require synthesis from the pflag dependency and from git's own CLI behaviour, neither of which is in the pinned tree. This is not an effort-based finding: the pinned tree is 66 tracked files, I read every flag-parsing path in command.go and grepped the whole tree for single-dash, POSIX and Go-flag-package handling.
